newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Asia-Pacific business urges China WTO membership.
newsitem.headline: Asia-Pacific business urges China WTO membership.

text.p: The Pacific Basin Economic Council (PBEC) meeting in Manila urged the World Trade Organisation (WTO) on Monday to accept China, the Russian Federation and Taiwan as members "at the earliest practical date".
PBEC is the oldest businessmen's organisation in the region, with more than 1,200 corporate members from 20 economies.

"Yesterday, the Board of Directors adopted a resolution urging the WTO to accept the applications of three PBEC member-economies that are not yet members of the WTO," Robert Lees, PBEC secretary general, said at the formal opening of the council's 30th international general meeting in the Philippine capital.
"PBEC expressed the need to fully bring these three important economies into the world trade system at the earliest practical date," he added.
PBEC chairman Gary Tooker, in a statement, said membership in the WTO creates responsibility among members to support and uphold the WTO's free trade policy.

"As the voice of business in the Pacific region and as one of the most powerful business orgnaisations in the Pacific, PBEC stands ready to support its applicant members with practical, technical assistance in joining the WTO," Tooker said.
